Assuming you mean **OLAP** (Online Analytical Processing) [S05-0138], here is what the course materials cover:

* **Definition:** OLAP stands for online analytical processing [S06-0204]. It is a data model that aggregates data to make querying across multiple dimensions easier and faster [S05-0138]. It is also described as a computer-based approach to analyzing data that enables users to extract and view data from multiple dimensions [S04-0210].
* **Purpose and Use:** OLAP databases are designed for putting in a lot of data and discovering hidden insights, and they are mainly used for analytical work by data analysts and data scientists [S06-0204]. They are mostly optimized for reading data and are primarily used for reporting and analysis [S05-0138], as well as in Business Intelligence (BI) applications [S04-0210]. 
* **Key Features:** 
  * It provides a multidimensional view of large volumes of data [S04-0210].
  * It aggregates data across multiple dimensions (such as time, location, product, and customer), helping users identify trends and relationships not easily visible in traditional two-dimensional views [S04-0210].
  * The data is periodically refreshed, and the data size is generally much larger compared to OLTP [S06-0205].
  * OLAP databases are denormalized for analysis [S06-0205].
* **Target Users:** OLAP increases productivity for data analysts and executives, and its users are knowledge workers such as data analysts, business analysts, and executives [S06-0205].
